subject: Operational continuity and operator on-call for air-gapped private deployment
messages:
From: Ava Sanchez <security-lead@nebulahealth.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@nebulahealth.com
Date: Sat, 11 May 2029 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Questions: operator on-call & failover for private (air-gapped) deploy

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security and ops teams need a short written response to a couple of operational continuity items before we can move to procurement review:

1) During an air-gapped private deployment, what is the on-call model for operator-level incidents? Do you support a 24/7 escalation path from our operators to Redwood on-call, or is the expectation that the customer will own on-call entirely? Please be explicit about responsibilities and expected RTOs for platform-level failovers.

2) Describe the automated and manual failover processes if a dedicated GPU node becomes unresponsive in a private VPC install. Are there health checks, automatic instance replacement, or a recommended operator runbook?

3) For scenarios where outbound connectivity is intentionally blocked (airgap), what telemetry/health channels are still available for operator diagnostics? What evidence artifacts can we expect (logs, runbooks) during audits?

Can you provide a short operator playbook and a network diagram that we can attach to our submission? A PDF is fine.

Security is on a tight timeline — procurement asked for the package by EOD Tuesday (US Pacific).

Appreciate it,

Ava Sanchez
Security Lead, Nebula Health
ava.sanchez@nebulahealth.com

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Sanchez <security-lead@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: procurement@nebulahealth.com, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 11 May 2029 12:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions: operator on-call & failover for private (air-gapped) deploy

Ava,

Thanks — appreciate the clear asks. Summary answers below and I've attached a concise operator playbook and a simplified VPC diagram as requested (attachments: operator_playbook_v2.pdf, vpc_network_diagram.png). High-level: Redwood supports both customer-owned on-call and several optional vendor-assisted escalation models (details and SLAs below).

1) On-call model and responsibilities
- Default: Customer-owned on-call. Your operators own first-response and remediation in air-gapped/private installs. Redwood provides a 24x7 vendor-on-call escalation path for critical platform defects or when engineering assistance is needed; that path is gated by a support-level activation (we can include in SOW).
- Typical flow: Customer operator triages -> if platform bug or runtime-level failure suspected -> open vendor escalation -> Redwood engineering assesses within 30 minutes and provides owner assignment.
- Target RTOs (vendor escalation): initial response 30 minutes; mitigation timeline varies by severity (SEV1: incremental mitigation steps within 4 hours; SEV2: 24 hours, with workaround guidance). These RTOs are configurable in Dedicated/Private SLAs.

2) Failover processes (private VPC / air-gapped)
- Health checks: Local agent runs node-level checks (GPU responsiveness, disk, network) with configurable probe frequency. Probe failures are logged locally to the operator agent and to on-disk circular logs when outbound is blocked.
- Automatic remediation (recommended default): On repeated health-check failure, the local orchestration layer attempts a soft-restart of the service and reloads KV cache; if that fails, it signals the operator console for manual intervention.
- Replacement: For Private installs with a supported orchestration layer (Kubernetes/nomad integrations), node replacement is handled by your cluster control plane using immutable image artifacts. For air-gapped sites where automated node replacement isn't possible, our operator playbook prescribes isolation, warm-spare routing, and manual image deploy steps (included in the attached playbook).
- Recommended operator runbook steps (summary): identify failure -> capture on-disk diagnostics -> attempt soft restart -> if unsuccessful, switch traffic to warm spare node (instructions in playbook) -> escalate to Redwood if error indicates platform regression.

3) Telemetry and audit artifacts with no outbound connectivity
- Local artifacts: structured logs, circular KV-cache snapshots, and per-request trace files are retained on the operator node (configurable retention window). We ship a small local diagnostic bundle tool (single binary) that operators can run to produce a zip with: recent logs, node metrics, kernel traces (optional), and a health-check report.
- Audit evidence: customer can export the diagnostic bundle and deliver via secure transfer (SFTP/physical media) for vendor analysis. We also provide signed attestations and a short diagnostic template your auditors can use to validate operator actions.

Attachments included:
- operator_playbook_v2.pdf (PDF, ~1.1MB): concise on-call playbook, escalation steps, sample operator commands for air-gapped remediation, and warm-spare activation checklist.
- vpc_network_diagram.png (PNG, ~340KB): simplified network topology showing allowed egress points, bastion/airlock patterns, and operator diagnostic paths.

Next steps: if you want, I can redact the playbook to remove any internal IDs and produce a version that maps to your org's runbook template. Also looping Marissa and Ben for SOW/SLA language and pricing for vendor-assisted 24x7 escalation.

Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Attachments: operator_playbook_v2.pdf (PDF), vpc_network_diagram.png (PNG)

From: procurement@nebulahealth.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, Ava Sanchez <security-lead@nebulahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 13 May 2029 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions: operator on-call & failover for private (air-gapped) deploy

Olga / Ava,

Thanks for the quick turnaround — procurement confirmed the attachments satisfy our initial packet. Two quick clarifications before we finalize the procurement worksheet:

- Is the vendor-assisted 24x7 escalation an add-on line item or included in Dedicated licensing? Please provide example SOW language and ballpark monthly cost for a single air-gapped site.
- For the diagnostic bundle tool, can we run it in unattended mode and have it write to a mounted NFS export on the operator console? Our security team wants to automate periodic snapshots.

If you can send those two items by EOD Tuesday we'll wrap the packet.

Regards,
Procurement Team
Nebula Health
procurement@nebulahealth.com

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@nebulahealth.com, Ava Sanchez <security-lead@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 May 2029 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions: operator on-call & failover for private (air-gapped) deploy

Procurement team — answers inline: 

- Vendor-assisted 24x7: offered as an add-on in Private engagements (we also offer it bundled for certain Enterprise contracts). I'll attach example SOW language below and include an indicative monthly cost for a single-site engagement: USD 12,500/month for 24x7 escalation (includes 1 named escalation engineer, on-call rotation, and quarterly playbook reviews). This is an indicative price — final depends on committed response SLA and number of warm-spare nodes.

SOW snippet (paste-ready): 
"Redwood will provide vendor-assisted escalation services to Nebula Health as an optional add-on. Services include: 24x7 point-of-contact for platform-severity incidents, vendor initial assessment within 30 minutes of escalation, remediation ownership where platform defects are identified, and quarterly operational reviews. Customer remains responsible for first-response operator activities and local node-level remediation per the Operator Playbook. Pricing is defined in the attached Schedule A."

- Diagnostic bundle automation: Yes — the diagnostic tool supports an unattended/daemon mode and can be configured to write outputs to a mounted NFS export or local USB as part of an automated snapshot policy. The tool respects file permissions and will encrypt the bundle with a customer-provided key when configured for automated export.

I'll produce a redacted playbook variant and a short SOW attachment by EOD. Looping Marissa for contract language and Ben for technical appendix details.

Thanks,
Olga
